segments: And his wife, his daughter, and that old woman remained in the house.
She took along her son and other young thieves,
and they came at night and entered the merchant's house,
and they stole everything.
And as they were leaving,
that old woman said with the merchant's wife:
"Blessed be God, who blinded their eyes so that they did not open the chest!"
And when the thieves heard this, they turned back and opened the chest,
and they took from it four thousand dinars, precious stones, and pearls, and left.
And Mas'ud and Da'ud met each other [in battle],
and Mas'ud was defeated,
and many of the men of his side were killed.
In this year, which is the year 1448
of the Greeks [1137 AD],
John, the king of the Greeks, set out in wrath against Leo the Armenian,
and he conquered Tarsus, Adana, and Mopsuestia.
And he also seized Leo himself, his wife, and his sons,
and sent them to Constantinople.
And he went and marched down against Antioch;
and when he was unable to capture it,
Joscelin came to him, and they agreed on the condition that when John took Aleppo and the rest of the cities of Syria and gave them to the Franks,
they would give him Antioch.
And they reached an agreement, and came and encamped against Aleppo,
and they captured the fortress of Buza'ah,
and they set siege engines against Shayzar.
Then Mas'ud, Sultan of Iconium, entered Cilicia,
and captured the city of Adana,
and took captive all the people and the bishop,
and they brought them as prisoners to Melitene.
Now King John, when he heard these things, burned the siege engines,
and returned to Cilicia,
and made peace with Mas'ud, the lord of Iconium,
and went to Constantinople.
And Malik Muhammad, the lord of Melitene, drove out his brother Dawlah (Dawlat?),
and took from him Ablistin and the region of Jayhan.
And Dawlah crossed over to Hanzith,
and from there to Amid,
and from there to Joscelin,
wandering about from place to place.
At this time the emir Isa,
the lord of Sibabarak,
which is Sabukht,
who was descended from Boghos {OCR?}, the Armenian who went to Baghdad and converted to Islam,
gathered an army,
and entered the region of Gargar to plunder.
And when he saw that the region was already devastated, he set his face against the monasteries and convents.
